newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SAirGroup expects higher 1997 oper profit.
newsitem.headline: SAirGroup expects higher 1997 oper profit.

text.p: SAirGroup said business in the first four months of 1997 had met or surpassed expectations so the company expected the full-year operating profit to markedly exceed that of 1996.

"All in all the first four months of 1997 have lived up to our expectations, in most areas the results even slightly exceed our rather high target, which means that -- excluding any unforeseen events -- we expect a markedly improved group operating result," SAirGroup chairman Hannes Goetz said.
The remarks were in the text of a speech prepared for the annual shareholders meeting.
In another part of his prepared speech Goetz also said the first four months of 1997 had "significantly surpassed expectations".

At its news conference in April SAirGroup had said business was on target, but it had not given a specific forecast for 1997. In 1996 SAirGroup operating profit rose 39.3 percent to 344 million Swiss francs, but extraordinary charges of 739 million pushed the net result into a loss of 497 million.
During the period from November 1996 through April 1997 the scheduled passenger traffic on the Swissair airline rose 11.9 percent to 4.479 million, SAirGroup chief executive Philippe Bruggisser said.

According to copies of his presentation materials the passenger load factor rose to around 70 percent at the end of April from around 65 percent the same period last year. -- Zurich Editorial +41 631 7340
